title: test(plugin-dashboard): settle the objectui#11417 TIE harness on a drawn legend, not on the bare surface (objectui#11459)
body:
Fixes #11459

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`renderChart` in `DatasetWidget.singleSeriesMeasures-11417.test.tsx` settled on `.recharts-surface` (or the renderer's `data-chart-error` notice) alone. It now also waits until every `recharts-legend-wrapper` the chart mounted holds its items. A chart that draws no legend mounts no wrapper and settles on the surface or the notice, as before. All four reads per type go through `renderChart`, so the settle covers `base`, `again`, `secondChanged` and `firstChanged`.

The determinism control is untouched and still compares the whole markup. Nothing was deleted, skipped or loosened. There is no retry and no fixed wait. The normaliser is unchanged, because the legend is part of what the TIE judges (see the `secondDrawn` flips below). Test-only, with one empty-frontmatter changeset.

## Mechanism, measured on `main` at `5988b6b53`

- Recharts `3.10.1` builds its store with Redux Toolkit's `autoBatchEnhancer({ type: 'raf' })`, and `addLegendPayload` is an auto-batched action. So the legend re-renders only when the store delivers its batched notification on the next animation frame. In happy-dom, `requestAnimationFrame` is a `setImmediate`.
- A pie mounts its surface and sectors in one commit. Its legend payload is computed from the registered graphical item and dispatched from a layout effect, so the legend items land one frame later. A timeline probe (a MutationObserver on the container, with `requestAnimationFrame` wrapped to count frames) recorded this for `pie`: one commit with the surface, 3 sectors and an EMPTY legend wrapper; then the first frame fires; then the wrapper holds `lost`, `open` and `won`.
- The harness's `waitFor` resolves on the commit that adds the surface, and RTL then drains with a `setTimeout(0)`. Whether that timer or the frame's `setImmediate` runs first depends on how long the current event-loop turn takes, which is load. That is why the read is usually settled and sometimes not.
- For all 13 types the TIE renders, every DOM state in which the surface (or notice) was present was compared with the settled markup. Only `pie` and `donut` ever showed a state that differed, and the difference was the legend wrapper's contents alone. Wherever the settled chart has a legend wrapper, it was already present in the first state with the surface. `funnel`, `treemap`, `sankey` and the `scatter` refusal never mount one.
- CI shows both directions, so any mount can miss the legend. Job 110807471565: `base` empty, `again` filled. Job 110837657193: `base` filled, `again` empty. Job 110843092024: `base` empty, `again` filled.

**Does the race reach the TIE itself, not only the control?** Yes. Of the 5 BASE failures below, 4 are at the TIE assertion, where `secondDrawn` read `true` for `pie` or `donut`: the legend landed in one of `base` / `secondChanged` and not the other. Only 1 is at the control. A per-read probe under the same load (16 copies, 832 reads) caught an empty legend in a `donut` `base` read, a `donut` `again` read and a `pie` `firstChanged` read. Each one filled in later. The `firstChanged` control cannot pass on the legend alone for these two types, because changing the first measure moves the sectors. No read on any type saw a wrapper that was absent at the read and present later.

## The pin: repeated run, red at BASE and green after

Load: 16 byte-identical copies of the file per vitest invocation, `--maxWorkers=8` on a 4-core container, running beside other agents' work (load average 7 to 10). Copies were untracked and removed after each run.

| Arm | Repeat count | Red files | Failed tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| BASE `5988b6b53` | 32 (2 invocations x 16) | 4 | 5 (4 at the TIE `secondDrawn` assertion, 1 at the control) |
| AFTER `bb131af46` | 32 (2 invocations x 16) | 0 | 0 |
| Ablation: the settle assertion deleted at `bb131af46` | 32 (2 invocations x 16) | 3 | 3 (2 TIE, 1 control) |
| Restore proof, after the ablation was restored | 16 | 0 | 0 |

The ablation ran through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. It recorded anchor hits going from 1 to 0 and blob `539bf762d20b` becoming `9baa6ef68998`, then on restore blob `539bf762d20b` equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

**Forced reproduction, as a deterministic second reading** (local only, never committed). Every other chart mount had its animation frames deferred by 30 ms through a wrapped `window.requestAnimationFrame`, which is the frame Recharts' store notifies on. Each arm ran 4 copies with `--maxWorkers=4`:

- BASE: 4 of 4 files red, 8 failed tests (the `pie` and `donut` control in every copy).
- AFTER: 0 of 4.
- Ablation: 4 of 4 red, 8 failed tests.

Deferring EVERY mount uniformly left BASE green (0 of 4): every read is then equally unsettled, so the control compares two empty legends and passes while the TIE judges half-drawn pies. The control can see this race only when two reads disagree. The settle is what keeps every reading on a finished chart.

## Siblings checked: none folded in

None of these compares two renders' markup:

- `DatasetWidget.chartConfigMarks-9203.test.tsx` has the same `.recharts-surface` settle. It reads sector fills, data labels and mark counts against literals and reads no legend. On a pie the sectors land in the same commit as the surface.
- `DashboardChart.chartConfigMarks-4044.test.tsx` has the same settle and also reads parts against literals. Its one legend read already waits for the legend text with its own `waitFor`. Its `showLegend: false` arm reads a wrapper that is never mounted.
- `DatasetWidget.dimensionlessMeasures-11261.test.tsx` settles on the surface, then reads axis ticks and waits for bar marks explicitly. Its `innerHTML` comparisons read a metric tile settled by `findByText`, with no Recharts involved.
- `DashboardChart.countSeriesKey-8266.test.tsx` names `.recharts-surface` only in prose. It asserts composed schema nodes, not markup.

## Local verification, all at `bb131af46`

- The repeated run above.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over all 36 `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DatasetWidget*` files printed `Test Files  36 passed (36)` and `Tests  389 passed (389)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. Its 12-package dependency closure was built first with turbo. `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`, and its `--listFiles` names the 11417 file.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` printed `check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 10035 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).`
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` printed `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only, exit 0`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exited 0: the one changeset has an empty frontmatter, which is the gate's exemption. `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals` all exited 0.
- ESLint was narrowed to the diff's one lintable file, the `.tsx` test.
  1. Population, read from ESLint's own config: `eslint --print-config` returns a config for that file (119 rules) and `undefined` for the changeset `.md`.
  2. File count, read from `--format json`: 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  3. Invariance: the effective config has no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`. Linting is not type-aware, so this diff cannot change any untouched file's result.
- Toolchain: installed with `pnpm install --config.engine-strict=false`, because the container's node v22.22.0 is below `jsdom@30`'s engines floor. No tracked file changed.

## Acceptance notes

- Observation, not filed: `DatasetWidget.dimensionlessMeasures-11261.test.tsx` reads `categoryTicks` straight after a surface settle. The probes here showed cartesian charts drawing their ticks and legend in the same commit as the surface, so that read is not exposed to this race today. Carrier: whoever next edits that file.
